name: Question 7
worked_solution:
First, we rewrite the polynomial, interpreting any constants as multiples of the identity matrix:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(X) & ={X}^{2}-4X+1 \\  & ={X}^{2}-4X+I\end{aligned}
$$

So, we want to find $f(K)={K}^{2}-4K+I.$

Let's calculate ${K}^{2}$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{K}^{2} & =K\cdot K \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 & 1 \\ 3 & 2\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}2 & 1 \\ 3 & 2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}7 & 4 \\ 12 & 7\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we can evaluate $f(K):$

$$
\begin{aligned}f(K) & ={K}^{2}-4K+I \\  & =[\begin{aligned}7 & 4 \\ 12 & 7\end{aligned}]-4[\begin{aligned}2 & 1 \\ 3 & 2\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}7 & 4 \\ 12 & 7\end{aligned}]-[\begin{aligned}8 & 4 \\ 12 & 8\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}7-8+1 & 4-4-0 \\ 12-12+0 & 7-8+1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$
